acquisition: The mass spectrometer was operated in a data-dependent mode
labeling: Quantification of cross-linked peptides was performed label-free
quantification: Quantification of cross-linked peptides was performed label-free using apQuant (3.1.1.27312) within Proteome Discoverer 2.3

workflow_hints: Cross-linking mass spectrometry (XL-MS) has emerged as a widely used tool for studying protein–protein interactions

Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a specialized Chemical Cross-Linking Mass Spectrometry (XL-MS) assay. While not explicitly in the provided modifier list as 'mod_xl', it aligns with the structural proteomics/protein-protein interaction goals of 'mod_tpp' (though TPP is specifically hydrogen-deuterium exchange, XL-MS is the primary method here). The use of DSBSO as a cleavable cross-linker is the central feature.

organism: Purified E. coli ribosome (E. coli B strain)
Purified recombinant Cas9 from S. pyogenes
cell_lines: spiked into a tryptic HEK background
scope: enrich azide-tagged, acid-cleavable disuccinimidyl bis-sulfoxide (DSBSO) cross-linked peptides using dibenzocyclooctyne (DBCO) coupled Sepharose beads
Enrichment of resulting cross-linked peptides using DBCO or BARAC biotin method
The prepared XL sample was mixed with equilibrated DBCO-beads
Elution of XL-peptides from the beads was performed by acidic cleavage

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The experiment focuses on the affinity enrichment of cross-linked peptides from purified proteins (Cas9 and E. coli ribosome). While HEK peptides were used as a background spike to mimic a cellular lysate, the analyzed material was specifically enriched via DBCO or streptavidin beads, fitting the 'affinity-purified complex scope'.

primary_biological_variables.matched_definition: Fallback category for studies where no clear perturbation or differential treatment axis is present in the proteomics comparison. This is not a mapping error when supported by evidence.
evidence: Here we describe an improved, easy to implement, one-step method to enrich azide-tagged, acid-cleavable disuccinimidyl bis-sulfoxide (DSBSO) cross-linked peptides using dibenzocyclooctyne (DBCO) coupled Sepharose beads.
Control samples, where no enrichment strategy was applied, were prepared and digested as explained above but not incubated to any beads

To compare the performance of the DBCO beads to an established enrichment method for DSBSO linked peptides, enrichment was alternatively also performed similarly, as described by Kaake et al. ... This method is indicated as “BARAC biotin method” within this publication.
While we detected up to 465 (XlinkX) unique cross-links on Cas9 after enrichment... in a control only 96 links were detectable
Compared to the BARAC-biotin approach we were able to get ∼5× increased cross-link numbers

Ontology_TreatmentAndDesign_prompt.notes: This is a method-development study focused on the efficiency of a peptide enrichment technique (DBCO beads vs BARAC-biotin vs no enrichment) rather than a biological perturbation study. Therefore, it is mapped as un-classified per the provided rules.

base_candidates_ranked.reason: Data-dependent acquisition (DDA) was used on Orbitrap instruments with label-free quantification (apQuant) for cross-linked peptide abundance.

modifier_candidates_ranked.reason: The experiment specifically uses DSBSO (disuccinimidyl bis-sulfoxide) as a chemical cross-linker, requiring specialized XL-MS search parameters and fragment ion detection.

special_reagent_hints: Linker specificity: Lysine and N-terminal amino residues

workflow: The mass spectrometer was operated in a data-dependent mode
Quantification of cross-linked peptides was performed label-free using apQuant
Cross-links were identified either using XlinkX 2.2 as nodes within Proteome Discoverer (2.3.0.523) or using MeroX (2.0.0.6)
differential: Control samples, where no enrichment strategy was applied, were prepared
To compare the performance of the DBCO beads to an established enrichment method
search_parameters: Carbamidomethyl (+57.021 Da) at cysteine was set as static modification
Oxidation (+15.995 Da) at methionine was set as dynamic modification
cross-link modification DSBSO was defined as C11H16O6S2
linker specificity toward lysine and N-terminal amino residues was set

Ontology_ProcessingAndDifferential_promp.notes: This is a specialized Chemical Cross-Linking (XL-MS) experiment. Standard bottom-up pipelines will fail to identify the cross-linked peptides without the specific DSBSO mass shifts and fragment ion logic (Alkene, Thiol, Sulfenic acid) used by XlinkX and MeroX.
